# `silk/crypto/aes_gcm`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Encrypt and authenticate data with AES-128-GCM, AES-192-GCM, or AES-256-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D).

## When to use
Use [`AesGcm.seal`](#AesGcm.impl.seal) to encrypt a message so that only holders of the key can read it and any
change is detected. Use [`AesGcm.open`](#AesGcm.impl.open) to check and decrypt it. If the protocol does not name
an algorithm, `silk.crypto.chacha20_poly1305` is also a good choice.

## Details
The key is 16 bytes (AES-128), 24 bytes (AES-192), or 32 bytes (AES-256). The nonce is usually
12 bytes; any other nonzero length is hashed into the first counter block, as NIST SP 800-38D
says. The tag is 16 bytes, or a prefix of 4, 8 or 12 to 15 bytes. The tag is separate from the ciphertext ("detached"), so store or send
both. The associated data (`aad`) is authenticated but not encrypted. Use it for headers that
must stay readable. The ciphertext has the same length as the plaintext. Nothing allocates.

When one key protects many messages, prepare it once with [`AesGcmKey`](#AesGcmKey), whose `seal` and
`open` skip the key schedule.

For data that arrives in parts, such as a stream or a Node.js `createCipheriv` call, use
[`AesGcmEncryptor`](#AesGcmEncryptor) and [`AesGcmDecryptor`](#AesGcmDecryptor). They take the message in any split, give the same
result, accept nonces of any nonzero length, and can write a truncated tag. On x86-64 they check
for AES-NI and PCLMULQDQ at run time, as [`AesGcm.seal`](#AesGcm.impl.seal) and [`AesGcm.open`](#AesGcm.impl.open) do, and then run
the counter mode and GHASH eight blocks at a time.

## Errors
The functions return an [`AesGcmError`](#AesGcmError). All checks come before the first write, and on any
error the output buffers do not change. [`AesGcm.open`](#AesGcm.impl.open) writes no plaintext unless the tag is
correct.

## Gotchas
The same key and nonce must never encrypt two messages. If they do, an attacker can recover the
XOR of the two plaintexts and forge tags. Use a counter, or 12 random bytes from
`silk.system.random` for a small number of messages per key.

Authentication does not stop replay: an attacker can send an old valid message again. The
functions do not erase their copies of the key.

## Examples
### Encrypt and decrypt a message
```silk
import silk.crypto.aes_gcm { AesGcm, AesGcmError }
import silk.core.result { Result }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let key: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  let nonce: [u8; 12] = [0; 12]
  let plaintext: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  let mut ciphertext: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  let mut tag: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  match AesGcm.seal(&key, &nonce, b"header", &plaintext, &mut ciphertext, &mut tag) {
    Result<(), AesGcmError>.Success { value: _ } => {}
    Result<(), AesGcmError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }

  // For this key and nonce, the ciphertext starts with 0388dace.
  if ciphertext[0] != 0x03 || ciphertext[1] != 0x88 {
    return 1
  }
  let mut decrypted: [u8; 16] = [1; 16]
  return match AesGcm.open(&key, &nonce, b"header", &ciphertext, &tag, &mut decrypted) {
    Result<(), AesGcmError>.Success { value: _ } => {
      if decrypted[0] != 0 || decrypted[15] != 0 {
        return 1
      }
      return 0
    }
    Result<(), AesGcmError>.Failure { error: _ } => 1
  }
}
```

### Detect a changed message
```silk
import silk.crypto.aes_gcm { AesGcm, AesGcmError }
import silk.core.result { Result }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let key: [u8; 32] = [7; 32]
  let nonce: [u8; 12] = [1; 12]
  let mut ciphertext: [u8; 5] = [0; 5]
  let mut tag: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  match AesGcm.seal(&key, &nonce, b"", b"hello", &mut ciphertext, &mut tag) {
    Result<(), AesGcmError>.Success { value: _ } => {}
    Result<(), AesGcmError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  ciphertext[0] = ciphertext[0] + 1
  let mut plaintext: [u8; 5] = [0; 5]
  return match AesGcm.open(&key, &nonce, b"", &ciphertext, &tag, &mut plaintext) {
    Result<(), AesGcmError>.Failure { error: AesGcmError.AuthenticationFailed } => {
      // The output does not change when the tag is wrong.
      if plaintext[0] != 0 {
        return 1
      }
      return 0
    }
    _ => 1
  }
}
```

Import as `AesGcm` with `import silk.crypto.aes_gcm { AesGcm }`.

<a id="AesGcm.impl.seal"></a>

### Associated function `seal`

```silk
pub fn seal(
    key: &[u8],
    nonce: &[u8],
    aad: &[u8],
    plaintext: &[u8],
    ciphertext: &mut [u8],
    tag: &mut [u8],
  ) -> Result<(), AesGcmError>
```

Encrypts `plaintext` into `ciphertext` and writes the authentication tag to `tag`.

The key is 16 bytes (AES-128), 24 bytes (AES-192), or 32 bytes (AES-256). The nonce is usually
12 bytes and can have any nonzero length. `tag` is 16 bytes for the full tag, or 4, 8 or 12 to
15 bytes for a prefix of it. `aad` is authenticated but not encrypted. Use it for headers that must stay readable.
The ciphertext has the same length as `plaintext`. `ciphertext` can be longer than
`plaintext`. The bytes after the written prefix do not change. The buffers must not overlap.
Nothing allocates.

#### Errors
All checks come before the first write. On an error, `ciphertext` and `tag` do not change.

- `InvalidKeyLength` if `key` is not 16, 24, or 32 bytes.
- `InvalidNonceLength` if `nonce` is empty or longer than 2^61 - 1 bytes.
- `InvalidTagLength` if `tag` is not 4, 8, or 12 to 16 bytes.
- `OutputTooSmall` if `ciphertext` is shorter than `plaintext`.
- `LimitExceeded` if `plaintext` is longer than 2^36 - 32 bytes or `aad` is longer than
  2^61 - 1 bytes.

#### Gotchas
Use a new nonce for each message under the same key. The function does not make one. If the
same key and nonce encrypt two messages, an attacker can recover the XOR of the two plaintexts
and forge tags. Use a counter, or 12 random bytes from `silk.system.random` for a small number
of messages per key. The function does not erase its copy of the key.

<a id="AesGcm.impl.open"></a>

### Associated function `open`

```silk
pub fn open(
    key: &[u8],
    nonce: &[u8],
    aad: &[u8],
    ciphertext: &[u8],
    tag: &[u8],
    plaintext: &mut [u8],
  ) -> Result<(), AesGcmError>
```

Checks `tag`, and if it is correct, decrypts `ciphertext` into `plaintext`.

The key is 16 bytes (AES-128), 24 bytes (AES-192), or 32 bytes (AES-256), and the nonce is the
one given to [`AesGcm.seal`](#AesGcm.impl.seal). `tag` is 16 bytes, or a prefix of 4, 8 or 12 to 15 bytes, which
is compared in constant time. `aad` must be the same bytes that were given to
[`AesGcm.seal`](#AesGcm.impl.seal). The function checks every tag byte before it writes `plaintext`. The bytes
after the written prefix do not change. Nothing allocates.

#### Errors
All checks come before the first write. On an error, `plaintext` does not change.

- `AuthenticationFailed` if the tag is not correct for the key, nonce, `aad`, and ciphertext.
- `InvalidKeyLength` if `key` is not 16, 24, or 32 bytes.
- `InvalidNonceLength` if `nonce` is empty or longer than 2^61 - 1 bytes.
- `InvalidTagLength` if `tag` is not 4, 8, or 12 to 16 bytes.
- `OutputTooSmall` if `plaintext` is shorter than `ciphertext`.
- `LimitExceeded` if `ciphertext` is longer than 2^36 - 32 bytes or `aad` is longer than
  2^61 - 1 bytes.

#### Gotchas
Authentication does not stop replay: an attacker can send an old valid message again. The
function does not erase its copy of the key.

<a id="AesGcmKey"></a>

## `AesGcmKey`

```silk
pub struct AesGcmKey
```

An AES-GCM key prepared once for many messages: its AES round keys and its GHASH key.

### When to use
Use it in place of [`AesGcm.seal`](#AesGcm.impl.seal) and [`AesGcm.open`](#AesGcm.impl.open) when one key protects many messages,
such as the records of a TLS connection. Each of those calls computes the key schedule again,
which costs about as much as encrypting a few hundred bytes.

### Details
[`AesGcmKey.seal`](#AesGcmKey.impl.seal) and [`AesGcmKey.open`](#AesGcmKey.impl.open) give the same output and errors as [`AesGcm.seal`](#AesGcm.impl.seal)
and [`AesGcm.open`](#AesGcm.impl.open) with the same key bytes. With a 12-byte nonce and a 16-byte tag on a machine
with the AES instructions, they use the prepared key. Otherwise they run the same code as those
functions. Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas
The value holds a copy of the key and its schedule, and does not erase them when it is dropped.
The rules for nonces are those of [`AesGcm.seal`](#AesGcm.impl.seal).

### Examples
```silk
import silk.crypto.aes_gcm { AesGcmError, AesGcmKey }
import silk.core.result { Result }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let key: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  let prepared = match AesGcmKey.make(&key) {
    Result<AesGcmKey, AesGcmError>.Success { value } => move value
    Result<AesGcmKey, AesGcmError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let nonce: [u8; 12] = [0; 12]
  let plaintext: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  let mut ciphertext: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  let mut tag: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  if let Result<(), AesGcmError>.Failure { error: _ } = prepared.seal(&nonce, b"header", &plaintext, &mut ciphertext, &mut tag) {
    return 1
  }
  // The same ciphertext as `AesGcm.seal` with this key and nonce.
  if ciphertext[0] != 0x03 || ciphertext[1] != 0x88 {
    return 1
  }
  let mut decrypted: [u8; 16] = [1; 16]
  return match prepared.open(&nonce, b"header", &ciphertext, &tag, &mut decrypted) {
    Result<(), AesGcmError>.Success { value: _ } => if decrypted[0] == 0 { 0 } else { 1 }
    Result<(), AesGcmError>.Failure { error: _ } => 1
  }
}
```

<a id="AesGcmEncryptor"></a>

## `AesGcmEncryptor`

```silk
pub struct AesGcmEncryptor
```

A streaming AES-GCM encryptor (NIST SP 800-38D) for a message that arrives in parts.

### When to use

Use it when the message does not fit in one buffer, or to implement an API that encrypts in
steps, such as `createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm")` in Node.js. For a message in one slice, use
[`AesGcm.seal`](#AesGcm.impl.seal).

### Details

Make one with [`AesGcmEncryptor.make`](#AesGcmEncryptor.impl.make) and the associated data, give the message with
[`AesGcmEncryptor.update`](#AesGcmEncryptor.impl.update), then call [`AesGcmEncryptor.finish`](#AesGcmEncryptor.impl.finish) for the tag. Any split of the
message gives the same ciphertext and tag as [`AesGcm.seal`](#AesGcm.impl.seal). The key is 16, 24, or 32 bytes.
The nonce can have any nonzero length: a 12-byte nonce is used directly, and other lengths are
hashed as NIST SP 800-38D section 7.1 says. Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas

The same key and nonce must never encrypt two messages. Prefer 12-byte nonces, which are the
only length that [`AesGcm.seal`](#AesGcm.impl.seal) takes. The value holds key material and is not erased when it
is dropped.

Returns an encryptor for `key` and `nonce` that authenticates the associated data `aad`.

`aad` is authenticated but not encrypted. Use it for headers that must stay readable. The
encryptor copies what it needs and does not borrow the arguments.

#### Errors

- `InvalidKeyLength` if `key` is not 16, 24, or 32 bytes.
- `InvalidNonceLength` if `nonce` is empty or longer than 2^61 - 1 bytes.
- `LimitExceeded` if `aad` is longer than 2^61 - 1 bytes.

Encrypts `plaintext` into the first `plaintext.length` bytes of `ciphertext`.

The bytes of `ciphertext` after them do not change. The buffers must not overlap.

#### Errors

On an error the state and `ciphertext` do not change.

- `OutputTooSmall` if `ciphertext` is shorter than `plaintext`.
- `LimitExceeded` if the message grows past 2^36 - 32 bytes.

<a id="AesGcmEncryptor.impl.finish"></a>

Writes the authentication tag to `tag` and consumes the state.

`tag` is 16 bytes for the full tag, or 4, 8, 12, 13, 14, or 15 bytes for a prefix of it, as
NIST SP 800-38D allows. Shorter tags are easier to forge.

#### Errors

- `InvalidTagLength` if `tag` has another length. `tag` does not change.

<a id="AesGcmDecryptor"></a>

## `AesGcmDecryptor`

```silk
pub struct AesGcmDecryptor
```

A streaming AES-GCM decryptor (NIST SP 800-38D) for a ciphertext that arrives in parts.

### When to use

Use it when the ciphertext does not fit in one buffer, or to implement an API that decrypts in
steps, such as `createDecipheriv("aes-256-gcm")` in Node.js. For a ciphertext in one slice, use
[`AesGcm.open`](#AesGcm.impl.open), which writes no plaintext unless the tag is correct.

### Details

Make one with [`AesGcmDecryptor.make`](#AesGcmDecryptor.impl.make) and the associated data, give the ciphertext with
[`AesGcmDecryptor.update`](#AesGcmDecryptor.impl.update), then call [`AesGcmDecryptor.finish`](#AesGcmDecryptor.impl.finish) with the received tag. The key
is 16, 24, or 32 bytes. The nonce can have any nonzero length. Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas

[`AesGcmDecryptor.update`](#AesGcmDecryptor.impl.update) writes plaintext before the tag is checked. Do not use or release
that plaintext until [`AesGcmDecryptor.finish`](#AesGcmDecryptor.impl.finish) succeeds. The value holds key material and is
not erased when it is dropped.

`aad` must be the same bytes that the encryptor got. The decryptor copies what it needs and
does not borrow the arguments.

#### Errors

- `InvalidKeyLength` if `key` is not 16, 24, or 32 bytes.
- `InvalidNonceLength` if `nonce` is empty or longer than 2^61 - 1 bytes.
- `LimitExceeded` if `aad` is longer than 2^61 - 1 bytes.

```silk

    (),
    AesGcmError
  >
```

Decrypts `ciphertext` into the first `ciphertext.length` bytes of `plaintext`.

The plaintext is not authenticated until [`AesGcmDecryptor.finish`](#AesGcmDecryptor.impl.finish) succeeds. The bytes of
`plaintext` after the written ones do not change. The buffers must not overlap.

#### Errors

On an error the state and `plaintext` do not change.

- `OutputTooSmall` if `plaintext` is shorter than `ciphertext`.
- `LimitExceeded` if the ciphertext grows past 2^36 - 32 bytes.

<a id="AesGcmDecryptor.impl.finish"></a>

### Method `finish`

```silk
pub fn finish(self: Self, tag: &[u8]) -> Result<(), AesGcmError>
```

Checks the received `tag` and consumes the state.

`tag` is the full 16-byte tag or a 4, 8, 12, 13, 14, or 15-byte prefix of it. The comparison
takes the same time wherever the bytes differ.

#### Errors

- `AuthenticationFailed` if the tag is not correct for the key, nonce, associated data, and
  ciphertext. Discard all plaintext that [`AesGcmDecryptor.update`](#AesGcmDecryptor.impl.update) wrote.
- `InvalidTagLength` if `tag` has another length.
